Hi Sofia,

Quick update from our side: the security team escalated the vendor risk assessment after their initial scan. They flagged inbound telemetry retention and encryption-in-flight specifics, and want an additional control narrative and a short architecture diagram before they sign off. That pushes our internal legal and procurement approvals out — earliest internal close is now 2026-09-21 instead of the end of August.

I attached the updated MAP and the redline from the security team. Can you confirm whether we can provide a short control narrative and a diagram by EOD Friday (8/21)? If not, please advise an alternative plan; procurement needs a decision by next Monday so they can finish budget approvals.

Thanks,
Jennifer

Hi Jennifer — thanks for the heads up and for attaching the redline. We can definitely produce a concise control narrative and a simple architecture diagram. I want to set expectations: 48 hours for the first draft, but we can compress to 24 hours if we include a short NDA-encumbered diagrams drop instead of fully polished docs.

Proposed immediate steps:
- We (Karthik + myself) will draft the control narrative and architecture diagram and share in a Drive link by 8/19 EOB PT.
- Marcus will coordinate an internal MAP update to preserve milestone gating for the evaluation plan (so procurement sees where the conditional go/no-go sits).
- If security requires additional evidence (logs, config snippets), we will request a scoped ask from them and provide an ETA for those artifacts.

If Acme can accept the draft narrative for an initial security review, we can keep the original close target of 8/31 for commercial sign-off and have a follow-up engineering checklist to finish by 9/07. If not, we will treat 9/21 as the re-baseline and document the decision log.

Which option do you prefer for procurement: accept draft narrative (keeps 8/31 in play) or re-baseline to 9/21 now?

Thanks,
Sofia

Subject: Re: MAP review — timeline impact (security gating)

Looping in here for mitigation planning. My take: push for the draft narrative now and request a scoped list of "must-have" evidence items from Acme security. Two tactical asks we can make to keep close near-term:
1) Provide a limited-time test instance with telemetry masking (we can supply masking rules) so their team gets a runbook and sample logs without full production retention exposure.
2) Offer a 1-week extension on evaluation access beyond contract signature (post-signature acceptance window) to give engineering time to finish config-level artifacts.

I can own the commercial note to procurement to preserve the 8/31 commercial close if Acme accepts the draft narrative option. If they insist on full artifacts before procurement moves, we will re-baseline to 9/21 and document impacts to rollout and billing start date.

Action items (internal):
- Karthik: can you draft the diagram + short narrative template? Aim for 8/19 noon.
- Sofia: prepare a procurement-facing one-pager explaining the conditional MAP gating and the acceptance criteria for the draft narrative option.

-Marcus
